outputs.L2: An optoelectronic semiconductor device is described. The device includes a semiconductor body (1) containing a layered semiconductor structure (2), which comprises a p-doped region (3), an n-doped region (5), and an active layer (4) positioned between these two regions. It further includes a plastic-containing carrier (10) provided with first and second through-connections (11, 12). A p-side contact layer (7) and an n-side contact layer (8, 8A) are disposed, at least in part, between the carrier (10) and the semiconductor body (1). The p-side contact layer (7) electrically couples the first through-connection (11) to the p-doped region (3), while the n-side contact layer (8, 8A) electrically couples the second through-connection (12) to the n-doped region (5). An electrostatic-discharge protection component (15) is also located between the carrier (10) and the semiconductor body (1). This protection component (15) is conductively connected to both through-connections (11, 12), and its forward-conduction direction is opposite to that of the layered semiconductor structure (2).
outputs.L3:
The optoelectronic component comprises a semiconductor body having a semiconductor layer sequence with a p-type region, an n-type region, and an active layer arranged between the p-type and n-type regions. The component further includes a plastic support containing first and second electrical vias.

A p-contact layer electrically connects the first via to the p-type region of the semiconductor body, while an n-contact layer electrically connects the second via to the n-type region. At least portions of the p-contact layer and the n-contact layer are arranged between the plastic support and the semiconductor body.

An electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection element is also positioned between the plastic support and the semiconductor body. The ESD protection element is electrically connected to both the first and second vias and is oriented anti-parallel to the semiconductor layer sequence. This configuration protects the optoelectronic component against potentially damaging electrostatic discharge events.
outputs.L4:
An optoelectronic semiconductor component comprises a semiconductor layer sequence arranged on a plastic support. The semiconductor layer sequence includes at least one p-type semiconductor region, at least one n-type semiconductor region, and an active layer located between the p-type and n-type regions. During operation, the active layer may generate electromagnetic radiation, detect electromagnetic radiation, or perform both functions. The semiconductor layer sequence may therefore form, for example, a light-emitting diode, a laser diode, or a photodetector.

Electrical contact with the semiconductor layer sequence is established by contact layers associated with the p-type and n-type regions. Conductive vias extend through at least part of the plastic support and connect the contact layers to external terminals or conductor structures. The vias permit the component to be contacted from the side of the plastic support facing away from the semiconductor layer sequence, thereby enabling a compact package design and simplifying integration into a circuit or carrier.

An electrostatic-discharge protection element is embedded in or otherwise integrated with the plastic support. The protection element is electrically connected between the conductive vias and is oriented anti-parallel to the diode structure formed by the semiconductor layer sequence. Under normal operating conditions, the ESD protection element remains nonconductive or has sufficiently high resistance that it does not materially affect the current flow through the active layer. The optoelectronic function of the component is therefore preserved.

If an electrostatic-discharge event applies a reverse voltage or other damaging transient across the terminals, the protection element becomes conductive and provides an alternative discharge path between the vias. The resulting current is diverted away from sensitive portions of the semiconductor layer sequence, reducing the voltage imposed on the active layer and associated junctions. Depending on the implementation, the protection element may comprise a diode, a semiconductor junction, a transistor-based protective structure, or another nonlinear device suitable for clamping transient voltages.

Embedding the ESD protection element in the plastic support avoids or reduces the need for a separate external protection component. It can also shorten the discharge path, decrease parasitic effects, and reduce the footprint of the finished device. At the same time, the use of vias and contact layers provides reliable electrical access to both sides of the semiconductor junction while allowing the plastic support to supply mechanical stability and electrical insulation where required.

The resulting component combines its optoelectronic function and electrostatic-discharge protection in a single compact structure. The anti-parallel connection ensures that the protective element responds preferentially to potentially harmful reverse-polarity events without interfering with the intended forward operation of the semiconductor layer sequence. This configuration improves robustness during fabrication, handling, assembly, and use while maintaining efficient operation and a small overall device size.
outputs.L5:
## ESD: Electrostatic Discharge

Electrostatic discharge (ESD) is the sudden transfer of electrical charge between two objects with different electrical potentials. It often occurs after static electricity builds up through friction—for example, when a person walks across a carpet and then touches a metal object. The resulting spark may be harmless to people, but it can seriously damage sensitive electronic components.

Modern microchips, circuit boards, and other semiconductor devices contain extremely small structures that can be harmed by an ESD event that a person may not even feel. Damage may cause immediate equipment failure or create hidden defects that shorten a product’s lifespan.

ESD protection is therefore essential in electronics manufacturing, repair, transport, and storage. Common preventive measures include:

- Wearing grounded antistatic wrist straps  
- Using ESD-safe work mats and tools  
- Storing components in antistatic bags or containers  
- Controlling workplace humidity  
- Wearing suitable protective clothing and footwear  
- Grounding equipment and work surfaces  
- Training employees in correct handling procedures  

An ESD-protected area, often called an EPA, is designed to reduce charge generation and safely dissipate static electricity. With appropriate equipment, procedures, and awareness, organizations can prevent costly failures, improve product reliability, and protect sensitive electronic devices.

An optoelectronic semiconductor device comprises a semiconductor body (1) having a semiconductor layer sequence (2). The semiconductor layer sequence (2) includes a p-conductive region (3), an active layer (4) configured to generate electromagnetic radiation during operation, and an n-conductive region (5), the active layer (4) being arranged between the p-conductive region (3) and the n-conductive region (5).

The semiconductor body (1) is disposed on a support (10). A first via (11) and a second via (12) are formed in the support (10) and provide electrical connection to a first contact (7) and a second contact (8), respectively. The first contact (7) is electrically coupled to the p-conductive region (3), and the second contact (8) is electrically coupled to the n-conductive region (5), such that electrical current can be supplied to the active layer (4).

An electrostatic-discharge protection element (15) is integrated in or arranged on the support (10) and is electrically coupled between the first and second contacts (7, 8). The electrostatic-discharge protection element (15) is configured to provide a discharge path upon application of an electrostatic overvoltage, thereby protecting the semiconductor layer sequence (2) from electrostatic-discharge-induced damage.

First and second through-support contacts (31, 32) extend through the support (3) and provide external terminals on its rear side. The anode (11) of the semiconductor chip (1) is electrically connected to the first through-support contact (31), and the cathode (12) is electrically connected to the second through-support contact (32), such that the chip’s forward direction extends from the first contact (31) to the second contact (32).
